comment: Liquid Dynamics surfaces. youngs_GPa is the modulus of the surface layer a glass object lands on; layer_mm is a compliant layer over a concrete substrate (carpet pile). splash_factor scales the splash threshold K = We^0.5 Re^0.25 > 57.7: rough surfaces splash more easily.

provenance.youngs_GPa: published: porcelain stoneware 50-70 GPa (ISO 10545 data; Dondi et al., J. Eur. Ceram. Soc. 2005)
provenance.absorbency: published: glazed surface, water absorption < 0.5% (ISO 13006 group BIa)

surfaces.name: Oak floorboards
surfaces.description: Lacquered hardwood: the glass lands across the grain.

provenance.youngs_GPa: estimated: red oak E_L 12.5 GPa with E_R/E_L 0.15 and E_T/E_L 0.08 (USDA Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, table 5-1); radial-tangential mean
provenance.absorbency: estimated: lacquer seals most of it

surfaces.name: Oak table top
surfaces.description: The table the glass stands on.

surfaces.name: Polished concrete
surfaces.description: Garage or loft floor: hard and a little rough.

provenance.youngs_GPa: published: normal-weight concrete 25-35 GPa (Eurocode 2, table 3.1, C30/37: 33 GPa)
provenance.splash_factor: estimated: rougher than tile, splashes earlier (Range & Feuillebois, J. Colloid Interface Sci. 203 (1998) 16)

surfaces.name: Cut-pile carpet
surfaces.description: Cut pile on a foam underlay over concrete: it catches the glass and drinks the wine.

provenance.youngs_GPa: estimated: effective compressive modulus of cut pile, ~0.3 MPa (carpet compression curves, ISO 3416)
provenance.layer_mm: estimated: 8 mm pile on a 6 mm underlay, typical residential

surfaces.name: Painted plasterboard
surfaces.description: An interior wall with matt emulsion.

provenance.youngs_GPa: published: gypsum board 2-3 GPa (Gypsum Association GA-235)
provenance.absorbency: estimated: matt paint takes up a little

surfaces.name: Window glass
surfaces.description: Float glass: the smoothest surface here; drops spread and run rather than splash.

provenance.splash_factor: estimated: smooth glass raises the splash threshold (Xu, Zhang & Nagel, PRL 94 (2005) 184505)

surfaces.name: Glassware
surfaces.description: The vessel's own glass, for its pieces striking each other and the liquid wetting it.

surfaces.name: Dummy skin
surfaces.description: The crash dummy's vinyl skin over its flesh simulant.

provenance.youngs_GPa: estimated: PVC skin over urethane flesh, a few MPa
